world.title: Pope Leo draws 650,000 in Córdoba, leads vigil for one million young people
world.summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass before an estimated 650,000 people in Córdoba on Nov. 10 and later led a prayer vigil in Buenos Aires attended by about one million young people, during the first papal visit to Argentina in nearly four decades. He is scheduled to celebrate his final Mass in Argentina in Luján on Wednesday
world.content: Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass before an estimated 650,000 people in Córdoba on Nov. 10 and later led a prayer vigil in Buenos Aires attended by about one million young people, during the first papal visit to Argentina in nearly four decades. He is scheduled to celebrate his final Mass in Argentina in Luján on Wednesday before flying to Peru, the last stop of his South American tour. In Córdoba, Leo urged worshippers to follow the example of Argentine saints and put faith into practice. He also met privately with about 20 people representing social causes, including Alba Camargo, a survivor of the 1976-1983 dictatorship whose relatives were forcibly disappeared. In Buenos Aires, Leo spoke about work, poverty and inclusion. Argentina’s Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno said the pope’s remarks challenged the country’s political and social leadership. On Tuesday night, Leo told young people not to let anyone take away their freedom, according to the Vatican.
world.image_alt: Pope Leo draws 650,000 in Córdoba, leads vigil for one million young people

world.title: US judge jails Meghan Markle’s father after ankle monitor removal
world.summary: A federal judge in Tampa, Florida, ordered Thomas Markle, the 82-year-old estranged father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, back into custody without bond on Nov. 10 after prosecutors said he cut off his court-ordered ankle monitor at 1:45 a.m. Markle had been released to home detention four days earlier, after his arrest
world.content: A federal judge in Tampa, Florida, ordered Thomas Markle, the 82-year-old estranged father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, back into custody without bond on Nov. 10 after prosecutors said he cut off his court-ordered ankle monitor at 1:45 a.m. Markle had been released to home detention four days earlier, after his arrest on one federal count of possessing child sexual abuse material. The charge followed an FBI search of two Los Angeles-area storage units Markle had rented since 2008. Prosecutors say agents seized about 78 items, including slides, film negatives and books, containing suspected abuse material. An FBI affidavit describes images investigators allege show Markle with children. Markle has denied possessing such images and called the allegations “sick lies”. U.S. Magistrate Judge Lindsay Saxe Griffin said Markle’s housing situation had become “untenable” and ordered a prompt medical evaluation. She also ordered that he be held separately from the general jail population where practicable. She had previously ordered a psychiatric examination to assess whether he is competent to stand trial, with a report due Nov. 20. Markle entered no plea at his initial hearing.
world.image_alt: US judge jails Meghan Markle’s father after ankle monitor removal

world.title: UK Privy Council strikes down Trinidad and Tobago ban on same-sex sexual activity
world.summary: The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council, Trinidad and Tobago’s final court of appeal, unanimously ruled on Nov. 10 that provisions of the country’s Sexual Offences Act cannot criminalize private, consensual sex between adults of the same sex. The decision overturned the remaining provisions following a challenge by
world.content: The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council, Trinidad and Tobago’s final court of appeal, unanimously ruled on Nov. 10 that provisions of the country’s Sexual Offences Act cannot criminalize private, consensual sex between adults of the same sex. The decision overturned the remaining provisions following a challenge by Trinidad-born activist Jason Jones and cannot be appealed. The five judges found that the provisions, enacted in a 1986 overhaul of sexual-offences law, were new legislation rather than protected colonial-era law. They ruled that the restrictions were not reasonably justifiable under the constitution’s protections for fundamental rights and private and family life. The ruling applies to Trinidad and Tobago, though campaigners say it could support legal challenges in other countries that retain similar laws. Jones said he plans targeted activism against homophobia across the Caribbean in the coming months. LGBTQ+ groups in Trinidad and Tobago say the judgment does not itself end discrimination in daily life.
world.image_alt: UK Privy Council strikes down Trinidad and Tobago ban on same-sex sexual activity

world.title: Rubio says no need for new Iran strikes as Hormuz talks continue
world.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Nov. 10 that President Donald Trump sees no need to resume major combat operations against Iran because U.S. sanctions and a naval blockade are inflicting growing economic damage. Rubio spoke after two days of Group of Seven foreign ministers’ talks in Paris and warned that U.S.
world.content: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Nov. 10 that President Donald Trump sees no need to resume major combat operations against Iran because U.S. sanctions and a naval blockade are inflicting growing economic damage. Rubio spoke after two days of Group of Seven foreign ministers’ talks in Paris and warned that U.S. forces remain ready if Iran crosses unspecified red lines. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran’s offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days still stands if Washington meets its conditions: ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the blockade of Iranian ports. Washington says nuclear issues must be included in initial negotiations. Rubio called Iran’s terms unrealistic, while Araghchi said sanctions and military action cannot end the war. Qatar and Pakistan are leading mediation, and Qatar’s prime minister joined European and Saudi diplomats for discussions in Paris. The status of direct negotiations remains disputed. Shipping attacks continued: an Emirati oil company reported damage to one vessel in United Arab Emirates waters, and a tanker reported a projectile strike off Oman. Crossings by loaded liquefied natural gas (LNG) tankers rose to 31 in October from 23 in September, according to vessel-tracking data cited by Dawn.

world.title: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent moves to military base after Iran threats
world.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has moved from his Washington-area home to a military base after threats against his life attributed to Iran, according to people familiar with the move cited by The New York Times and Reuters. The specific threats and their severity have not been publicly detailed. U.S. officials
world.content: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has moved from his Washington-area home to a military base after threats against his life attributed to Iran, according to people familiar with the move cited by The New York Times and Reuters. The specific threats and their severity have not been publicly detailed. U.S. officials have assessed that Iran’s capacity for large-scale attacks in the United States is limited, but treat specific threats against individuals as serious. Iran has denied plotting attacks against U.S. officials and people on American soil. Bessent leads President Donald Trump’s financial pressure campaign against Tehran, called Operation Economic Outcast, which began in August and operates alongside a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports. A senior administration intelligence official warned in a memo seen by Reuters late last month that Iranian plots against U.S. personnel and citizens had reached an “advanced stage”. A source familiar with Bessent’s move said security concerns rose after an aerial photograph of his Georgetown home made its location identifiable. The Treasury Department said Bessent would continue the campaign. U.S. officials have not publicly disclosed details of the threats.
world.image_alt: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent moves to military base after Iran threats

world.title: UK comedian David Walliams named in sexual misconduct allegations
world.summary: British comedian and children’s author David Walliams was named on Nov. 10 in a joint investigation by The Guardian and ITV News. Multiple women alleged that he used his celebrity status to pursue them when they were teenagers or young adults. One woman said he sexually assaulted her at his home when she was 15; anothe
world.content: British comedian and children’s author David Walliams was named on Nov. 10 in a joint investigation by The Guardian and ITV News. Multiple women alleged that he used his celebrity status to pursue them when they were teenagers or young adults. One woman said he sexually assaulted her at his home when she was 15; another said they first met when she was 15 and had sex when she was 17. Walliams denies the allegations and says he did not abuse his position. The reports followed a three-year investigation and a failed legal bid to prevent publication. London’s High Court rejected Walliams’ injunction request on Nov. 3, finding that publication would increase his suicide risk but that the evidence did not establish that suicide was inevitable. His identity remained protected until the appeal deadline passed on Nov. 9. The court did not determine whether the allegations were true. The Metropolitan Police contacted the two news organizations to explain how potential victims could report possible criminal allegations; no charges had been brought, ABC News reported. The BBC began removing some programmes featuring Walliams, and his literary agency said it would no longer represent him. Producers of the forthcoming film Fing removed his cameo, while UK distributor Sky said it would drop the film.
world.image_alt: UK comedian David Walliams named in sexual misconduct allegations

world.title: Nvidia taps Wachtell lawyer to investigate CEO amid China spy claims
world.summary: Nvidia has hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead an independent investigation into whether Chinese intelligence targeted chief executive Jensen Huang after he acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip customer Megaspeed. Wachtell partner Joon H. Kim, a
world.content: Nvidia has hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead an independent investigation into whether Chinese intelligence targeted chief executive Jensen Huang after he acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip customer Megaspeed. Wachtell partner Joon H. Kim, a former acting U.S. attorney, will lead the inquiry; the FBI is conducting a separate investigation. Access to restricted artificial-intelligence chips and the handling of intelligence warnings are also under scrutiny. Taiwan’s immigration chief said Alice Huang entered the island on a Hong Kong passport; Taiwan’s interior minister, Liu Shyh-fang, said her entry permit had been revoked and Taiwan would review screening procedures. A report cited by NDTV alleged that a network linked to Alice Huang facilitated at least $7.5 billion in Nvidia chip imports to Chinese companies since 2023; the claim has not been established. Nvidia’s board has said it has no reason to believe company secrets or U.S. national security were compromised, while a shareholder lawsuit accuses the company and Huang of misleading investors about the relationship and related risks. The board’s independent committee, assisted by outside counsel, is conducting the company review as lawmakers seek a closed-door briefing with Huang.
world.image_alt: Nvidia taps Wachtell lawyer to investigate CEO amid China spy claims

world.title: US charges three men over alleged Iran-linked UK airbase plot
world.summary: The U.S. Justice Department charged three men on Nov. 10 over an alleged plot to attack RAF Fairford, a British air base used by U.S. forces, and their alleged involvement in other attacks. The defendants are Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, a dual Iranian-Iraqi national; Mohsen Mohajeri, an Iranian national; and M
world.content: The U.S. Justice Department charged three men on Nov. 10 over an alleged plot to attack RAF Fairford, a British air base used by U.S. forces, and their alleged involvement in other attacks. The defendants are Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, a dual Iranian-Iraqi national; Mohsen Mohajeri, an Iranian national; and Mohammad Ali al-Hassani, an Iraqi national. Prosecutors allege they acted in support of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and the Iraqi armed group Kata'ib Hezbollah. The eight-count indictment says al-Hassani organized British associates, arranged for vans carrying fuel and made other preparations, while al-Saadi sent coded messages through relatives from a New York jail. Prosecutors allege the vans were meant to explode at the base; British police found no explosives but seized fuel. Only al-Saadi is in U.S. custody; prosecutors have not disclosed the other two men’s whereabouts. The indictment also links the defendants to nearly 20 alleged attacks or attempted attacks against Jewish communities and other targets in Europe and North America. The U.S. withdrew its B-1 bombers from Fairford after the September incident; Iran has denied involvement.
world.image_alt: US charges three men over alleged Iran-linked UK airbase plot

business.title: Fed governor warns AI investment shortfalls could trigger sharp stock declines
business.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Michelle Bowman warned that disappointing returns on artificial-intelligence investment could trigger sharp stock declines, weaken consumer spending and increase pressure on interest-sensitive sectors. Technology shares have been volatile since Democrats’ Nov. 3 U.S. midterm election victory ra
business.content: Federal Reserve Governor Michelle Bowman warned that disappointing returns on artificial-intelligence investment could trigger sharp stock declines, weaken consumer spending and increase pressure on interest-sensitive sectors. Technology shares have been volatile since Democrats’ Nov. 3 U.S. midterm election victory raised concerns about regulation and data-center construction: stocks sold off on Nov. 5, then rebounded on Nov. 9. Investors are weighing whether heavy infrastructure spending can generate returns before computing equipment loses value. Amazon said faster technological advances led it to shorten the estimated useful life of some servers and networking equipment from six years to five in 2025, increasing depreciation and amortization by $1.4 billion and cutting net income by $1 billion. Morgan Stanley called the selloff excessive and advised buying the decline, while other analysts warned that borrowing, customer concentration and equipment replacement could undermine returns. Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly results on Nov. 17.
business.image_alt: Fed governor warns AI investment shortfalls could trigger sharp stock declines

business.title: SoftBank reports $7.1 billion loss after US data-center writedown
business.summary: SoftBank Group reported a ¥1.12 trillion ($7.1 billion) net loss for the three months through September, its first quarterly loss in almost two years, after recording a $3.7 billion charge on advance payments for equipment intended for U.S. AI data centers. The company said revised procurement plans and changing projec
business.content: SoftBank Group reported a ¥1.12 trillion ($7.1 billion) net loss for the three months through September, its first quarterly loss in almost two years, after recording a $3.7 billion charge on advance payments for equipment intended for U.S. AI data centers. The company said revised procurement plans and changing project requirements led to the charge; declines in holdings including Arm, Intel and Coupang also weighed on results. SoftBank is reviewing its equipment procurement but said its large Ohio data-center project remains on track and is not being downsized. The company is revising the project’s contract. Chief Financial Officer Yoshimitsu Goto said the company could receive rebates of up to $2.1 billion on future equipment purchases, subject to conditions. SoftBank’s shares have fallen more than 50% from their June peak, and the company increasingly relies on debt to finance its AI investments.
business.image_alt: SoftBank reports $7.1 billion loss after US data-center writedown

business.title: AI cloud provider CoreWeave raises 2026 forecast, limits unsecured borrowing
business.summary: U.S. artificial-intelligence cloud provider CoreWeave reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion, up 168% from a year earlier and above analyst expectations, and raised its 2026 revenue forecast to $13 billion-$13.3 billion. The company also said it expects to become profitable on an adjusted basis in the first ha
business.content: U.S. artificial-intelligence cloud provider CoreWeave reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion, up 168% from a year earlier and above analyst expectations, and raised its 2026 revenue forecast to $13 billion-$13.3 billion. The company also said it expects to become profitable on an adjusted basis in the first half of 2028. Investors have questioned whether CoreWeave can finance its rapid data-center expansion as borrowing costs rise. Chief Financial Officer Nitin Agrawal said the company does not plan to issue additional unsecured parent-level debt through 2027 at current yields and expects less than $5 billion in parent-level debt financing over that period. Chief Executive Mike Intrator said customer prepayments and hardware-partner financing would cover most of its funding needs for 2027, with new contract-backed debt planned in the coming weeks.
business.image_alt: AI cloud provider CoreWeave raises 2026 forecast, limits unsecured borrowing

business.title: Oil rebounds near $92 as tanker attacks temper Iran peace bets
business.summary: Oil prices rose Wednesday after a two-day slide, with Brent reaching $92.53 a barrel as traders reassessed prospects for an end to the US-Iran war and attacks continued on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The conflict has disrupted regional oil flows. President Donald Trump has played down further strikes, but no
business.content: Oil prices rose Wednesday after a two-day slide, with Brent reaching $92.53 a barrel as traders reassessed prospects for an end to the US-Iran war and attacks continued on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The conflict has disrupted regional oil flows. President Donald Trump has played down further strikes, but no peace deal has been confirmed. The rebound followed Tuesday’s settlement at two-month lows: Brent closed at $91.49 and US West Texas Intermediate at $86.04. Iran’s top security official, Mohsen Rezaei, said there were no negotiations between Tehran and Washington, while attacks on vessels continued. Higher producer output and a global surplus have also put downward pressure on prices.
business.image_alt: Oil rebounds near $92 as tanker attacks temper Iran peace bets

business.title: U.S. gasoline average falls below $4 as crude retreats
business.summary: The U.S. average for regular gasoline fell to $3.9788 a gallon on Nov. 10, dipping below $4 for the first time since July. Prices were about 17 cents lower than a week earlier and nearly 39 cents lower than a month earlier, according to AAA data reported by CNBC. Brent crude briefly dropped below $90 a barrel as Presid
business.content: The U.S. average for regular gasoline fell to $3.9788 a gallon on Nov. 10, dipping below $4 for the first time since July. Prices were about 17 cents lower than a week earlier and nearly 39 cents lower than a month earlier, according to AAA data reported by CNBC. Brent crude briefly dropped below $90 a barrel as President Donald Trump said he was not looking to escalate the Iran conflict and Gulf oil flows recovered. Seasonal factors also contributed to the decline: demand typically weakens in colder months, and stations switch to a cheaper winter gasoline blend. October’s consumer price index rose 0.4% from September, while the increase in energy prices slowed to 0.7% from 5.2% in September. Diesel remained around $6.15 a gallon, and Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller cautioned that energy shocks may continue to affect inflation depending on how long prices stay elevated. GasBuddy petroleum analyst Patrick De Haan said the national gasoline average could reach $3.75 by Thanksgiving if geopolitical conditions do not disrupt the trend.
business.image_alt: U.S. gasoline average falls below $4 as crude retreats

business.title: Tech donors raised nearly $425 million in campaign against California billionaire tax
business.summary: Economists and labor advocates dispute why California voters rejected Proposition 40, a proposed one-time 5% tax on billionaires to fund healthcare and other services. The Associated Press called the measure’s defeat on Nov. 9, after ballots from the Nov. 3 election were counted. The debate centers on whether wealthy d
business.content: Economists and labor advocates dispute why California voters rejected Proposition 40, a proposed one-time 5% tax on billionaires to fund healthcare and other services. The Associated Press called the measure’s defeat on Nov. 9, after ballots from the Nov. 3 election were counted. The debate centers on whether wealthy donors’ advertising drove the result or voters opposed the tax itself. Economist Gabriel Zucman said the anti-tax spending could have been pivotal, while Stanford economist Joshua Rauh argued that voters in affluent Bay Area counties were especially skeptical, suggesting the policy—not just campaign spending—mattered. Opponents raised nearly $425 million, compared with just over $31 million for the campaign backed by SEIU-United Healthcare Workers West, according to The Guardian. The union said it may return with a tax proposal in 2028 if state leaders do not protect patients or find another healthcare funding solution.
business.image_alt: Tech donors raised nearly $425 million in campaign against California billionaire tax

business.title: Nvidia shares slide as CEO probe and inflation fears rattle investors
business.summary: Nvidia shares fell 5.5% on Tuesday after dropping 4.3% Monday, putting more than $470 billion of market value at risk over two sessions as investors weighed an internal investigation involving CEO Jensen Huang and broader concerns about artificial intelligence (AI) spending. Reports allege that Huang had a relationship
business.content: Nvidia shares fell 5.5% on Tuesday after dropping 4.3% Monday, putting more than $470 billion of market value at risk over two sessions as investors weighed an internal investigation involving CEO Jensen Huang and broader concerns about artificial intelligence (AI) spending. Reports allege that Huang had a relationship with a Chinese businesswoman suspected by U.S. authorities of espionage. Nvidia’s board has opened an investigation, and the FBI is examining whether Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. Reuters has not independently verified the allegations. A hotter U.S. inflation reading also pressured technology shares: consumer prices rose 0.4% in October from the previous month, and market pricing put the chance of a Federal Reserve rate increase in December at about 90%. The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.74% Tuesday, while Nvidia’s market value stood at around $4.07 trillion after the two-day decline. Nvidia is scheduled to report earnings on Nov. 17.
business.image_alt: Nvidia shares slide as CEO probe and inflation fears rattle investors

business.title: U.S. household debt reaches $19.1 trillion as delinquencies edge up
business.summary: U.S. household debt rose $334 billion, or 1.8%, to a record $19.1 trillion in the third quarter, while the share of debt at least 30 days overdue increased to 5% from 4.7% in the second quarter, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York said. Credit card balances also reached a record of about $1.29 trillion, while mortgage
business.content: U.S. household debt rose $334 billion, or 1.8%, to a record $19.1 trillion in the third quarter, while the share of debt at least 30 days overdue increased to 5% from 4.7% in the second quarter, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York said. Credit card balances also reached a record of about $1.29 trillion, while mortgages continued to account for most household debt. The overall level of delinquent debt remained consistent with pre-pandemic conditions, and the New York Fed said the rise in early mortgage and auto delinquencies had not weakened overall mortgage credit quality. Rates of transition into serious delinquency declined for credit cards and student loans, though the share of student loans more than 90 days overdue rose to 10.9% from 10.6% in the prior quarter. New York Fed economic research advisor Donghoon Lee said new credit-card delinquencies could continue to decline in the absence of macroeconomic shocks.
business.image_alt: U.S. household debt reaches $19.1 trillion as delinquencies edge up

science.title: Simulations link Uranus and Neptune’s skewed magnetic fields to interior conditions
science.summary: Computer simulations based on Voyager 2 measurements suggest that increasing electrical conductivity with depth inside Uranus and Neptune may explain their unusually tilted, off-center magnetic fields. The study, led by Chi Yan of the University of Texas at Austin, was published Nov. 3 in Communications Physics. The mo
science.content: Computer simulations based on Voyager 2 measurements suggest that increasing electrical conductivity with depth inside Uranus and Neptune may explain their unusually tilted, off-center magnetic fields. The study, led by Chi Yan of the University of Texas at Austin, was published Nov. 3 in Communications Physics. The models indicate that the fields may also shift substantially over decades, unlike Earth’s comparatively steady magnetic tilt. Researchers are using observations of faint auroras from the James Webb Space Telescope to track the planets’ magnetic environments; NASA has prioritized a Uranus mission for the early 2040s.
science.image_alt: Simulations link Uranus and Neptune’s skewed magnetic fields to interior conditions

science.title: Brazil presents voluntary fossil fuel exit roadmap at COP31
science.summary: Brazil presented a voluntary roadmap at the U.N. climate talks in Antalya on Nov. 10, setting out ways countries can plan a transition away from coal, oil and gas. The toolkit covers fossil-fuel demand, production and supply, and the economic effects of changing energy systems; it is not a binding agreement. U.N. Secre
science.content: Brazil presented a voluntary roadmap at the U.N. climate talks in Antalya on Nov. 10, setting out ways countries can plan a transition away from coal, oil and gas. The toolkit covers fossil-fuel demand, production and supply, and the economic effects of changing energy systems; it is not a binding agreement. U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres urged governments to create national plans with clear timelines and financing needs, and to show measurable progress by 2028. Power projects are waiting for grid connections, while high borrowing costs make renewable infrastructure harder to finance in many developing economies. Guterres said the European Union had incurred more than €100 billion in additional fossil-fuel import costs since the current Middle East escalation began. Negotiators are expected to continue discussing how to finance the transition and reflect it in national plans ahead of the 2028 global climate review.
science.image_alt: Brazil presents voluntary fossil fuel exit roadmap at COP31

science.title: NASA opens astronaut applications for lunar and Mars exploration missions
science.summary: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) has opened applications for a new astronaut class, seeking U.S. citizens to train for future missions to the Moon and, eventually, Mars. Applications are due by 11:59 p.m. Eastern time on Dec. 3, and the advertised annual salary is $164,395. The recruitment will
science.content: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) has opened applications for a new astronaut class, seeking U.S. citizens to train for future missions to the Moon and, eventually, Mars. Applications are due by 11:59 p.m. Eastern time on Dec. 3, and the advertised annual salary is $164,395. The recruitment will expand the astronaut corps for NASA’s Artemis lunar program, including missions near the Moon’s south pole and longer-term plans for a lunar base. Applicants generally need a STEM master’s degree, at least three years of related professional experience and the ability to pass a long-duration spaceflight physical; specified doctoral, medical and test-pilot qualifications can also meet the education requirement. NASA expects to announce its selections by late 2027. Those selected will complete about two years of training before becoming eligible for spaceflight assignments.
science.image_alt: NASA opens astronaut applications for lunar and Mars exploration missions

science.title: Study dates Taung Child to 3 million years, questions fossil classification
science.summary: A new study dates the Taung Child, a South African hominin fossil, to between 2.96 million and 3.03 million years ago—older than a previous estimate of 2.58 million—and argues that fossils long grouped as Australopithecus africanus may represent more than one species. Researchers compared tooth and brain development an
science.content: A new study dates the Taung Child, a South African hominin fossil, to between 2.96 million and 3.03 million years ago—older than a previous estimate of 2.58 million—and argues that fossils long grouped as Australopithecus africanus may represent more than one species. Researchers compared tooth and brain development and found differences between the Taung Child and other fossils from the region. The team hypothesizes that repeated shifts between wet and dry climates changed habitats, sometimes isolating hominin populations and sometimes bringing them into contact. Fossilized pollen indicates the Taung Child lived in a wetter, more wooded setting than the area’s present-day landscape.
science.image_alt: Study dates Taung Child to 3 million years, questions fossil classification

science.title: Three research teams report new ways to control and probe magnetism
science.summary: Researchers reported three separate findings on controlling or probing magnetism, from a single atom to quantum materials. At Delft University of Technology, a team led by physicist Sander Otte used radio-frequency signals to flip the magnetic spin of an individual atomic nucleus. The spin responded even when its coupl
science.content: Researchers reported three separate findings on controlling or probing magnetism, from a single atom to quantum materials. At Delft University of Technology, a team led by physicist Sander Otte used radio-frequency signals to flip the magnetic spin of an individual atomic nucleus. The spin responded even when its coupling to the electron could not explain the effect; the physical mechanism remains unknown. At the U.S. Department of Energy’s Ames National Laboratory, researchers found they could switch the handedness of magnons, magnetic excitations that carry information through materials, by changing a material’s magnetic state. Separately, Oak Ridge National Laboratory researchers used laser pulses and neutron measurements to detect a long-lived magnetic state that violated detailed balance, a rule governing energy-gaining and energy-losing events in systems at rest. The findings appeared in Nature Communications and Physical Review Letters.
science.image_alt: Three research teams report new ways to control and probe magnetism

science.title: Arctic ice cores trace century-old toxic pollution to Montana mine
science.summary: Researchers traced arsenic and other heavy metals preserved in 10 Arctic ice cores to the Anaconda Copper Mine in Montana, linking pollution to a single industrial source thousands of kilometers away. Arsenic levels in some cores reached about 15 times preindustrial levels around 1914, according to the study in Nature
science.content: Researchers traced arsenic and other heavy metals preserved in 10 Arctic ice cores to the Anaconda Copper Mine in Montana, linking pollution to a single industrial source thousands of kilometers away. Arsenic levels in some cores reached about 15 times preindustrial levels around 1914, according to the study in Nature Sustainability. By combining ice-core measurements, atmospheric modeling and historical production records, the team estimated that about 50.5 million Americans and 600,000 Canadians were exposed to arsenic levels associated with increased health risks between 1898 and 1918. Pollution-control equipment installed at the smelter in 1919 reduced emissions by roughly 60% to 65%, though the mine continued operating until 1947. Lead researcher Joseph McConnell, a climate and environmental scientist at the Desert Research Institute, said epidemiologists should investigate the pollution’s potential effects on people.
science.image_alt: Arctic ice cores trace century-old toxic pollution to Montana mine

science.title: Hubble image highlights dwarf galaxy’s role in distributing heavy elements
science.summary: NASA featured a Hubble Space Telescope image of the dwarf galaxy NGC 4449 on Nov. 11, noting that the galaxy and others like it contain less oxygen than models predict. The discrepancy suggests stellar winds and supernova explosions can expel oxygen and other heavy elements from these galaxies, scattering material that
science.content: NASA featured a Hubble Space Telescope image of the dwarf galaxy NGC 4449 on Nov. 11, noting that the galaxy and others like it contain less oxygen than models predict. The discrepancy suggests stellar winds and supernova explosions can expel oxygen and other heavy elements from these galaxies, scattering material that helps form stars and planets. The image shows regions of young stars, dark dust lanes and pink gas clouds, according to the Macedonian report. NASA describes dwarf galaxies as roughly one-tenth the Milky Way’s size and among the most common galaxy types. The featured image comes from an existing Hubble observation, not a newly reported one.
science.image_alt: Hubble image highlights dwarf galaxy’s role in distributing heavy elements

science.title: NASA studies show LISA could detect planets through gravitational waves
science.summary: Two studies led by NASA astrophysicists describe how the planned Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) could detect exoplanets orbiting pairs of white dwarfs through the planets’ effects on gravitational-wave signals. Such detections would reveal a population not yet observed: planets around binary white dwarfs. LI
science.content: Two studies led by NASA astrophysicists describe how the planned Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) could detect exoplanets orbiting pairs of white dwarfs through the planets’ effects on gravitational-wave signals. Such detections would reveal a population not yet observed: planets around binary white dwarfs. LISA is scheduled to launch in the mid-2030s, and researchers estimate the Milky Way contains about 10 million double-white-dwarf systems with orbital periods under an hour. The studies also describe how NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope could help verify candidate planets. The findings appeared in The Astrophysical Journal.
science.image_alt: NASA studies show LISA could detect planets through gravitational waves

sports.title: Arsenal
sports.summary: Arsenal midfielder Martin Zubimendi has denied reports that he is close to a move, as Chelsea, Real Madrid and Atlético Madrid monitor his situation. The 27-year-old has yet to start a Premier League match this season after losing his place amid competition from summer signing Bruno Guimarães and Myles Lewis-Skelly. Zu
sports.content: Arsenal midfielder Martin Zubimendi has denied reports that he is close to a move, as Chelsea, Real Madrid and Atlético Madrid monitor his situation. The 27-year-old has yet to start a Premier League match this season after losing his place amid competition from summer signing Bruno Guimarães and Myles Lewis-Skelly. Zubimendi said manager Mikel Arteta had explained before the season that new arrivals would mean competition for minutes. He said he remains patient and hopes his role can change. Arsenal still consider him a useful squad option and are not reported to be pushing for a sale, though the club may need a significant departure to fund a winger in January. Reports say Arsenal would seek at least the £60 million they paid Real Sociedad in 2025. The transfer window opens in January, but no negotiations are reported to be advanced.

sports.content: Czech Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova became the first player to reach the WTA Finals semifinals on Tuesday, beating American Coco Gauff 6-3, 6-3 in Indian Wells, California. The 21-year-old has won both Group 1 matches in straight sets on her tournament debut; Gauff, the world No. 4, has yet to qualify. American Jessica Pegula kept her semifinal bid alive by beating Ukrainian alternate Marta Kostyuk 6-2, 7-5. Kostyuk, who joined the field after world No. 1 Elena Rybakina withdrew with a viral illness, is eliminated after two losses. Thursday’s final Group 1 matches will decide the remaining semifinal place: Pegula faces Noskova, while Gauff meets Kostyuk. Noskova has already advanced, but the final group standings remain undecided.

sports.content: Scotland midfielder Scott McTominay has revealed that doctors treated his irregular heartbeat under anaesthetic two days before the team’s World Cup opener against Haiti in June. He played in all three of Scotland’s matches, but the team exited in the group stage after losing to Morocco and Brazil. McTominay said the episode affected him mentally after the tournament, though he did not offer it as an excuse for Scotland’s performances. After the heart rhythm problem recurred while he was playing for Napoli, he underwent cardiac ablation in Manchester in September and missed all four of Scotland’s first Nations League matches under new head coach Sébastien Pocognoli. He says he now feels much better and has returned to Scotland’s squad for its final Nations League fixtures this month. McTominay has played in all nine of Napoli’s matches since the last international break; Scotland host North Macedonia on November 13 and visit Switzerland on November 16.

sports.content: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has returned to the club’s Säbener Straße training complex for the first time since he collapsed while observing a reserve-team session on Oct. 23. The 40-year-old was hospitalized with meningeal irritation, an inflammation of the membranes around the brain and spinal cord, and is now receiving treatment for a shoulder injury he suffered in the fall. Bayern said he was “on the road to recovery”. Assistant coach Aaron Danks led Bayern to four wins and one draw in five matches during Kompany’s absence. Kompany spent six days in hospital, and Bayern have not confirmed when he will return to the touchline. Bayern’s next match is at home against Cologne on Nov. 20, after the international break. Honorary president Uli Hoeneß has predicted Kompany will be back on the bench for that game, while Danks said the break gives the club time to assess when Kompany is ready.

sports.content: The Indianapolis Colts kept star running back Jonathan Taylor at Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline despite receiving offers that included at least a second-round draft pick. The team wanted a “blockbuster” return. The New York Giants’ reported offer of second- and fifth-round picks was withdrawn. Taylor, 27, remains with the 2-7 Colts, who have traded several veteran starters. He has rushed for 656 yards and eight touchdowns this season. The Colts also kept quarterback Daniel Jones. Their next general manager will have a say in Taylor’s future, and the team could revisit a trade in the offseason.

sports.content: Mumbai Indians have traded captain and all-rounder Hardik Pandya to Punjab Kings for left-arm fast bowler Arshdeep Singh ahead of the 2027 Indian Premier League (IPL) season, the league confirmed on Wednesday, November 11. The direct swap values each player at ₹18 crore, raising Pandya’s fee from ₹16.35 crore. The teams dropped an option to include Punjab reserve wicketkeeper Vishnu Vinod. The move ends Pandya’s second stint with Mumbai and Arshdeep’s eight-season tenure with Punjab. Arshdeep leaves as Punjab’s leading IPL wicket-taker, with 111 wickets in 96 matches. Pandya captained Gujarat Titans to the 2022 title and the 2023 final. Mumbai now has a captaincy vacancy; Punjab is expected to retain Shreyas Iyer as captain. Teams must submit their lists of retained and released players by November 17, ahead of the mini-auction scheduled for December 16 in Goa.

Publisher Penguin said the book tour would continue, with changes t
sports.content: Former Australia batter Usman Khawaja has withdrawn from some scheduled interviews promoting his autobiography after declining to say whether current captain Pat Cummins and other bowlers knew about the 2018 ball-tampering plan he says the team shared. Publisher Penguin said the book tour would continue, with changes to this week’s schedule rather than a full cancellation. In an ABC interview, Khawaja said he had given his account in the book and would not name individuals or directly answer questions about Cummins. Fast bowler Mitchell Starc again denied prior knowledge, saying his recollection was unchanged from a 2021 joint statement by Australia’s Cape Town bowlers. Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg says the conflicting accounts do not justify reopening the inquiry, while the Australian Cricketers’ Association has urged an end to personal attacks. Stand-in one-day captain Mitchell Marsh is expected to speak on Thursday, ahead of Australia’s first one-day international against England on Friday.

sports.title: Formula One drops Imola backup, keeps Qatar and Abu Dhabi as final races
sports.summary: Formula One has told Italy’s Imola circuit it will not be needed as a contingency venue, keeping the final two 2026 races in Qatar on November 27-29 and Abu Dhabi on December 4-6. The schedule remains unchanged after conflict-related disruption earlier this season: Saudi Arabia’s race was cancelled and Bahrain’s was mo
sports.content: Formula One has told Italy’s Imola circuit it will not be needed as a contingency venue, keeping the final two 2026 races in Qatar on November 27-29 and Abu Dhabi on December 4-6. The schedule remains unchanged after conflict-related disruption earlier this season: Saudi Arabia’s race was cancelled and Bahrain’s was moved to Malaysia. Formula One says conditions in Qatar and Abu Dhabi have not worsened in recent months, travel advice still permits visits and teams support the plan. Mohammed Ben Sulayem, president of the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), said the sport is prepared to hold both events. The Las Vegas Grand Prix, scheduled for November 20-22, comes first. Formula One says it will prioritise safety and could cancel the Gulf races if the situation deteriorates. With Imola no longer serving as a backup, Las Vegas could become the season’s final race if the last two rounds cannot be held.
